classification.difficultyReason: Combine the two soldier counts, use the constant soldier-days product to find the new duration, and subtract it from 20 days to answer how much less time the food lasts.

content.prompt: An army bunker currently has 60 soldiers and enough food to last them 20 days. They are joined by 40 more soldiers. Assuming inverse variation, how much less time will their food supply last?

answer.short: 8 days less; the food lasts 12 days.
answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the number of days the food lasts for 100 soldiers. The product of the number of soldiers and the duration is constant.
$$\begin{align*}100t&=60\times20\\100t&=1200\\t&=12.\end{align*}$$
The food lasts $20-12=8$ days less.
